scope: Operations-only review of Cloudflare ownership, publication authority, and deployment-evidence boundaries; no deployment, DNS, credential, automation, schedule, or canonical queue mutation performed.

phases.claim_or_design_tested: The repository has a coherent, currently assigned Cloudflare responsibility that can safely guide architectural or deployment work.
challenge_method: Read operations/CURRENT_STATE.json and operations/ACTIVE_QUEUE.json from preview.
Compared canonical queue ownership with recent Cloudflare implementation, test, queue, and evidence commits.
Sought provider-role conflicts, duplicate publication authority, stale ownership, and unsupported deployment assumptions.
evidence: CURRENT_STATE identifies Vercel capacity and immutable Vercel deployment verification as the active deployment boundary.
ACTIVE_QUEUE contains Vercel Studio, Continuity Mining, and Frontier Research items but no Cloudflare-owned active item.
Recent Cloudflare commits establish publication-boundary tests, output enforcement, canonical test binding, and evidence artifacts.
Existing Cloudflare evidence explicitly states that source contracts do not prove a live Cloudflare deployment or hostname.
failures_or_counterexamples_found: A mature Cloudflare code and evidence surface can coexist with no canonical Cloudflare queue assignment.
Historical Cloudflare queue commits do not establish that the responsibility remains active in the current canonical queue.
Treating the committed Cloudflare controls as current deployment authority would conflict with CURRENT_STATE and Vercel-owned publication policy.
Starting architecture or deployment work from team-title intent alone would create architecture drift and duplicate provider authority.
repairs_made: Kept Cloudflare fail-closed and non-authoritative for publication.
Restricted this cycle to an additive evidence record rather than modifying canonical queue state or provider configuration.
Defined queue ownership and immutable provider evidence as separate prerequisites: neither may be inferred from historical commits.
remaining_uncertainty: Whether Cloudflare is intended to own DNS, edge controls, fallback delivery, archival mirroring, or no active production role.
Whether a superseded or omitted Cloudflare queue object exists outside the accessible canonical queue.
Whether any Cloudflare account or project is currently linked to this repository.
phases.rollback_route: Revert the commit that adds this evidence-only artifact; no runtime or canonical state changed.
phases.next_falsifiable_step: Resolve Cloudflare ownership through one explicit canonical queue item or an explicit no-active-role decision before any provider architecture or deployment experiment.

phases.claim_or_design_tested: Adding another validator or provider integration would strengthen the system in this cycle.
challenge_method: Compared the identified ownership defect with existing publication-boundary and output-enforcement controls.
Tested the competing explanation that missing enforcement, rather than missing authority, was the primary gap.
Evaluated whether a new validator would produce independent safety value or duplicate existing policy.
evidence: The repository already contains Cloudflare publication-boundary and publication-enforcement tests bound to a canonical command.
The unresolved fact is organizational authority and provider identity, not absence of another source-level guard.
No immutable Cloudflare project or deployment object was available to validate.
failures_or_counterexamples_found: Another validator would not answer who owns Cloudflare work or whether Cloudflare is linked to the repository.
A new integration could pass source tests while still targeting the wrong project, branch, build output, or provider role.
Writing a Cloudflare queue item without authoritative intent would mutate shared planning state based on inference.
repairs_made: Rejected duplicate implementation and speculative queue mutation.
Recorded the authority gap as the primary defect and preserved reversibility.
Kept existing Cloudflare controls intact and made no production-facing change.
remaining_uncertainty: The canonical Cloudflare test command was not executed in this connector-only cycle.
No consumer inventory proves every Cloudflare publication path uses the canonical gate.
No authoritative Cloudflare provider metadata was inspected.
phases.next_falsifiable_step: After ownership is explicitly resolved, inventory all Cloudflare publication-path consumers and execute the canonical contract suite at the exact preview commit.

phases.claim_or_design_tested: Cloudflare work is verified, deployable, publishable, or promotable based on the current repository evidence.
challenge_method: Required current canonical ownership, immutable provider identity, exact commit agreement, branch mapping, generated hostname, quota and cancellation state, rollback evidence, and successful canonical test execution.
Applied non-success classification to absent, queued, canceled, skipped, superseded, rate-limited, stale, and commit-mismatched deployment states.
Constructed counterexamples in which source controls are green while provider ownership or deployment identity is absent or wrong.
evidence: No Cloudflare-owned item is present in the current ACTIVE_QUEUE.
No immutable Cloudflare deployment object, project identifier, commit-matched hostname, branch mapping, DNS authority, quota state, or rollback execution evidence was available.
The active repository deployment state remains fail-closed around Vercel verification.
failures_or_counterexamples_found: A passing source contract cannot prove current team authority.
A historical queue commit can be stale or superseded by the canonical queue.
A valid Cloudflare deployment could still be non-authoritative if Vercel remains sole publication owner.
A generated hostname or alias without exact commit and branch agreement can represent stale or mismatched content.
repairs_made: Blocked Cloudflare deployment, publication, and promotion claims.
Separated four gates that must all pass: canonical ownership, provider-role non-conflict, source-level enforcement, and immutable deployment evidence.
Retained missing, stale, canceled, skipped, superseded, rate-limited, and commit-mismatched evidence as non-success.
remaining_uncertainty: Cloudflare's intended role and authority remain unresolved.
Provider account linkage, project configuration, branch mapping, domain authority, quota state, and cancellation history remain unknown.
Canonical tests and rollback behavior were not executed in this cycle.
phases.rollback_route: No deployment or shared-state mutation occurred; revert this evidence-only commit if removal is required.
phases.next_falsifiable_step: Obtain an explicit canonical ownership decision, then perform read-only Cloudflare project reconciliation before any disposable non-production deployment fixture is considered.

strongest_surviving_design: Use a four-gate Cloudflare boundary: (1) an explicit current canonical ownership assignment or explicit no-active-role decision, (2) a non-overlapping provider role relative to Vercel, (3) source-level publication enforcement through the canonical Cloudflare contract suite, and (4) immutable commit- and branch-matched provider deployment evidence with quota, cancellation, hostname, and rollback status. Failure or absence at any gate blocks publication and promotion.
rejected_alternatives: Infer active Cloudflare authority from the automation title or historical Cloudflare commits.
Add another overlapping validator before resolving ownership.
Mutate ACTIVE_QUEUE based on inferred intent.
Treat source-level test binding as live deployment evidence.
Allow Cloudflare and Vercel to publish the same surface without explicit ownership, precedence, and rollback semantics.
Trigger a deployment to discover configuration.
unresolved_risks: No current canonical Cloudflare owner or queue item.
Unknown Cloudflare account and project linkage.
Unknown branch, build-command, output-directory, hostname, DNS, quota, cancellation, and rollback state.
Canonical Cloudflare tests not executed at the exact evidence commit.
Potential stale historical Cloudflare planning artifacts.
